en: When nothing is ready to merge, a pull request from a `release/record-` branch that waits for a missing required check is looked at on the forge: if it is open at the head decided on, was opened by the workflow's token, is older than a two-minute grace and has not a single check of its own, the executor closes it with a comment saying why and reopens it at once. It does so once per head, under the integration lease, with `reopen_attempted` on the trail before the forge is asked and `reopened` or `reopen_failed` after, and `--dry-run` only names it. A record a person opened, one that already has a run of its own, one still inside the grace, and every other branch are left alone. A reopen that fails after the closure says the pull request was left closed and names the command a person runs. Left to the owner, because it changes the release pipeline and case <n1/>: the dispatch of validate in `.github/workflows/release.yml` is redundant once the executor reopens the record (both runs then validate the same head), and it stays until the owner removes it.
cs: Když není nic připraveno ke sloučení, pull request z větve `release/record-`, který čeká na chybějící povinnou kontrolu, se na forge prověří: je-li otevřený na rozhodnuté hlavě, otevřel ho token workflow, je starší než dvouminutová odklad a nemá jedinou vlastní kontrolu, executor ho uzavře s komentářem, proč, a ihned znovu otevře. Dělá to jednou na hlavu, pod zámkem integrace, s `reopen_attempted` ve stopě před dotazem na forge a `reopened` nebo `reopen_failed` po něm, a `--dry-run` ho jen pojmenuje. Záznam otevřený člověkem, záznam, který už má vlastní běh, záznam ještě v odkladu i všechny ostatní větve zůstanou nedotčeny. Znovuotevření, které po uzavření selže, řekne, že pull request zůstal uzavřený, a uvede příkaz, který člověk spustí. Ponecháno vlastníkovi, protože mění release pipeline a případ <n1/>: dispatch validate v `.github/workflows/release.yml` je nadbytečný, jakmile executor záznam znovu otevírá (oba běhy pak validují stejnou hlavu), a zůstává, dokud ho vlastník neodstraní.

Prompts typed on the web, in the desktop application, on another machine, or into a provider with no adapter are not observable from a hook that was never run, and none of them appear here. Only Claude Code has an adapter. The question this sentence used to defer — whether Codex or Gemini has an equivalent event — was settled on 2026-09-11 and the answer is that both do: Codex CLI fires <t1/> before model invocation and Gemini CLI fires <t2/>, each handing the raw prompt to a command, each citable in <t3/>. They are therefore <t4/> — this distribution ships no adapter — and not <t5/>, which would be a false statement about their products (ADR <n1/>). Prompt capture over the MCP connection is not a substitute and is declared impossible: a server is handed tool calls, never the prompt that produced them.

Every capability carries its effect in the registry: a read, a change to the answering runtime's own state (the peer board, the mesh journal, the evidence ledger), or a change to the repository. There is no authentication and no remote binding by default; the server is for the clients on this machine. When it is bound beyond loopback, its reads answer whoever reaches it, and every capability that changes something is refused to a remote caller unless a linked node signed the input. It does not run a model and it does not route work to one.
